newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices steady to down, demand soft.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices steady to down, demand soft.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, pressured by sluggish East Coast utility demand, were steady to down slightly Friday, but trade was extremely thin ahead of the U.S. Labor Day holiday on Monday, sources said.
"The big move (up) in crude (recently) stemmed the bearish tide, but the market feels sloppy. There's no demand," said one cash trader, noting cheaper gas continued to siphon load.
New York Harbor prompt one percent slipped another 25 cents to $16.75 a barrel, with Sept paper unchanged at $16.85-95 and Oct up slightly with crude at $17.25-40, traders said.
NYMEX will be closed Monday for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
NYH Nov and Dec paper also were steady to up slightly at $17.65-85 and $18.10-35, respectively. Q1 was talked at $18.10-30, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH were little changed.
"High sulphur may provide a floor. Mexicans are still buying," a trader said.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent was 25-50 cents lower at $15.75-16.00, with ENEL spec about a quarter higher.
USG three percent was steady at $14.50-75, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate September gas prices lost more than five cents to about the $1.90/mmBtu level versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.66/mmBtu equivalent.
